verdict_reason: The exact application - phone photo of a varroa tray/sticky sheet -> automated computer-vision detection-and-count -> infestation level for the treat/no-treat decision - is already deployed in both open-source software (VarroDetector, YOLOv11-nano, validated R2~0.98-0.99) and multiple commercial apps (Apizoom, BeeScanning, Varroa Counter on Google Play). Molmo2's point-and-count is merely a newer model class for a problem that vision teams have demonstrably already targeted and shipped.

prior_art_found: Sygyt Software (sygyt.com) and Overtone Analyzer - dedicated tools explicitly used for studying/teaching overtone singing via real-time spectrogram + pitch detection: https://www.sygyt.com/en/ and https://overtone-analyzer.updatestar.com/en

MeionSpector / VoceVista / SING&SEE - real-time overtone visualization feedback loops where learners watch harmonic bands and adjust vocal-tract shaping: https://techfortheclassicalsinger.wordpress.com/2012/07/28/spectrogram-apps-for-visualizing-the-overtones-in-your-voice/

30+ year mature field of ML/DNN automatic singing assessment with real-time pitch/spectral feedback: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.12153v1 ; plus GVPT guided visual pitch tracking: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.00750
lukemcraig/OvertoneFilter - existing harmonic-emphasis tool for sygyt-style overtones (DSP, not learned separation): https://github.com/lukemcraig/OvertoneFilter

SAM-Audio's own paper documents a limitation separating highly similar sources (overtones are highly similar), and ML is only now releasing isolated overtone datasets - so a learned drone/overtone separator-for-pedagogy is not yet shipped: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.18099 and https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/new-dataset-release-overtone-singing-preview-articulation-level-overtone-throat-singing-primitives/171144
verdict_reason: The underlying pedagogical capability - making the invisible overtone observable in real time for corrective vocal-tract feedback - is already well-served by spectrogram/pitch-tracking tools explicitly built for teaching overtone singing (Sygyt Software, Overtone Analyzer, MeionSpector, VoceVista, SING&SEE), so the domain problem is NOT untouched. However, none of these perform learned audio source separation into a listenable isolated overtone stem; that specific SAM-Audio framing (promptable two-source drone/overtone separation) is a genuinely new, untried angle - making this a qualified first-mover rather than open or closed. (Caveat: SAM-Audio's paper flags weakness on highly similar sources, which overtones are.)
